name: redis — facts about the codebase that are not in the codebase
how_these_were_chosen: Each case asks something the current source cannot answer: whether a change was undone, and which issue or pull request a behaviour came out of. Reading redis at HEAD tells you what the code does; none of these tell you why it is that way.

The expected evidence is a commit sha, a pull request number or an issue number taken from the repository's own history, so a pass means the answer cited something a reader can open — not that the wording sounded right.
Run with --baseline. A case the empty graph also passes was answerable from the question itself and does not belong in the suite.

cases.question: why was sendfile removed from redis replication?
cases.note: Implemented, then reverted on 2020-06-06. HEAD contains no sendfile, so the code cannot say it was ever tried.

cases.question: was the scan command performance change for matching data type kept?
cases.note: Reverted 2025-01-13; the optimisation is absent from HEAD, which reads the same as never having existed.

cases.question: why does GETRANGE behave the way it does — was an improvement reverted?
cases.note: PR #12272 landed and was then reverted.

cases.question: what happened to the optimization of memory usage for deferred replies?
why does geohash output 11 characters instead of 10?
cases.note: A change to 10 characters was reverted in 2019, which is why the code shows 11.

cases.question: which pull request fixed the SA_ONSTACK problem under Cygwin?
why does redis create a PID file even when running in the foreground?
cases.note: Issue #463 asked for it; the behaviour is in the code, the reason is not.

cases.question: why is SORT ordered the way it is when called against lists with zero ordering?
